title: Kill Chain Taxonomy for LLM Attacks: Adapting MITRE ATLAS to Structured Red-Teaming

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: The mapping from cyber kill chain to LLM attack phases is conceptually useful for systematizing red-teaming, but the impact chain is indirect: producing a taxonomy and dataset helps defenders prioritize but does not itself close vulnerabilities.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: MITRE ATLAS is publicly available, and implementing representative attacks using Garak/AISafetyLab is feasible. However, implementing attacks across all kill chain stages and producing a structured dataset is a significant engineering effort for beginners in 30 hours.

narrow_scope.reasoning: The project spans 6-7 attack stages, each requiring a representative implementation, plus data collection, measurement, and visualization. This is a broad survey project rather than a tightly scoped experiment.

novelty.reasoning: MITRE ATLAS already provides exactly this taxonomy. As of October 2025, it contains 15 tactics, 66 techniques, 46 sub-techniques, 26 mitigations, and 33 real-world case studies structured as an attack lifecycle from reconnaissance through impact. In October 2025, MITRE collaborated with Zenity Labs to add 14 new techniques specifically for AI Agents and GenAI. ATLAS Navigator and Arsenal provide free tools for threat modeling and red teaming. The NIST CSRC presentation (Sept 2025) details the framework's alignment with kill chain methodology. The proposed idea — mapping a cyber kill chain to LLM attack phases and building a dataset — is the exact purpose and current state of MITRE ATLAS.

MITRE ATLAS.details: Confirmed at atlas.mitre.org. 15 tactics, 66 techniques, 46 sub-techniques, 33 case studies as of Oct 2025. Directly implements the proposed taxonomy.

Garak/AISafetyLab.details: Garak confirmed as open-source LLM vulnerability scanner. Relevant as implementation tool but not the core contribution.
